Answer: C
Reason: The chest X-ray reveals a large, dense opacity in the left upper lung zone with ill-defined margins and blunting of the costophrenic angle (suggesting effusion/hemothorax) in the context of acute trauma; this appearance is characteristic of a retained radiopaque foreign body (such as wood, which can appear dense when wet or contaminated) causing penetrating lung injury, rather than typical contusion, pneumonia, or atelectasis.
